rows.speaker: مجاهد، قتادة بن النعمان، عكرمة، ابن جريج
rows.claim: These authorities relate the preceding incident: a woman carried the man's load on her head, cast it at al-Abṭaḥ, and complained that he had brought her nothing good, citing poetry by Ḥassān.
rows.anchor: هذا قول مجاهد وقتادة بن النعمان وعكرمة وابن جريج إلا أن عكرمة قال

rows.speaker: عكرمة وابن عباس
rows.claim: They say Banū Ubairiq planted the stolen property on a Jew, Zayd ibn al-Suhaym, and asked the Prophet to argue for them; he intended to do so and punish the Jew before revelation came.
rows.anchor: إن بني أبيرق طرحوا ذلك على يهودي يقال له: زيد بن السهين فجاء اليهودي إلى رسول الله

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says an Anṣārī who had entrusted armor was falsely accused of denying it; his clan sought the Prophet's support, and the verses came after the Prophet defended him as apparently innocent.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: نزلت في رجل من الأنصار استودع درعا فجحد صاحبها

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers the entrusted-armor account because betrayal properly concerns a deposit, whereas theft is not betrayal in this sense.
rows.anchor: واختار الطبري هذا الوجه قال لأن الخيانة إنما تكون في الوديعة لا في السرقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God says He sent the Qur'an in truth, meaning with what God is due from His servants; another gloss is that Muḥammad is more entitled to it.
rows.anchor: الذي يجب لله على عباده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is to judge among people by what God has shown him, that is, what God taught him in His Book.
rows.anchor: أي أعلمك الله في كتابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet must not defend someone who betrayed a Muslim or a protected non-Muslim in person or property against the party seeking the right that was violated.
rows.anchor: نهاه أن يكون لمن خان مسلما أو معاهدا في نفسه أو ماله خصيما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command asks the Prophet to seek God's forgiveness for having argued on behalf of the traitor; God forgives and spares Muslim servants punishment for their sins.
rows.anchor: أمره بأن يستغفر الله في مخاصمته عن الخائن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although addressed to the Prophet, the admonition is for his community: he defended someone who appeared just and faithful but was inwardly otherwise; God is exalted above all sins and indecencies.
rows.anchor: والخطاب وإن توجه إلى النبي من حيث خاصم عمن رآه على ظاهر الإيمان والعدالة وكان في الباطن بخلافه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another account says the Prophet did not actually defend the accused; he only intended to, and God reproached him for that intention.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنه لم يخاصم عن الخصم وإنما هم بذلك فعاتبه الله عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse follows the discussion of hypocrites and disbelievers with a command to avoid defending traitors; another connection is that, after legal rulings, it affirms that all were sent in truth.
rows.anchor: وجه اتصال الآية بما قبلها أنه لما تقدم ذكر المنافقين والكافرين والأمر بمجانبتهم عقب ذلك بذكر الخائنين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another account of the connection is that after explaining the rulings and laws in the sūra, God states that all of them were sent in truth.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنه تعالى لما بين الأحكام والشرائع في السورة عقبها بأن جميع ذلك أنزل بالحق

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو، حمزة، قتيبة، الكسائي، سهل، خلف، الباقون
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr, Ḥamza, Qutayba, al-Kisāʾī, Sahl, and Khalaf read the verb with yāʾ; the rest read it with nūn. Yāʾ follows the preceding third-person clauses, while nūn matches what follows.
rows.anchor: قرأ فسوف يؤتيه بالياء أبو عمرو وحمزة وقتيبة والكسائي وسهل وخلف والباقون بالنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamm is what one intends or resolves to do; related words include himma (aspiration) and hammām (a king of great aspiration).
rows.anchor: الهم ما هممت به ومنه الهمة

rows.speaker: علي بن عيسى
rows.claim: ʿAlī ibn ʿĪsā defines najwā in ordinary language as speaking privately.
rows.anchor: علي بن عيسى: النجوى هو الإسرار

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says najwā is speech set apart by a group or two people, whether secret or spoken openly.
rows.anchor: الزجاج: النجوى في الكلام ما ينفرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Najawtu can mean to strip or remove something; a poet uses it of taking a hide off an animal.
rows.anchor: ومعنى نجوت الشيء في اللغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Najawtu someone can also mean to smell or test their breath, as in the cited poem about smelling Mujālid.
rows.anchor: ونجوت فلانا إذا استنكهته قال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Najwā derives from najwa, elevated ground; a confidant is a najī and a group in private consultation are anjiyya.
rows.anchor: وأصله من النجوة وهو ما ارتفع من الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parsing makes man genitive: the sense is except in the private conversation of someone who enjoins good.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون من في موضع جر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second parsing makes man an accusative, disconnected exception: rather, there is good in the private talk of one who commands charity or recognized good, seeking God's pleasure.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون استثناء ليس من الأول ويكون موضعها نصبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third parsing puts man in the genitive by attachment to kathīr; here najwā means the people consulting, as in the phrase idh hum najwā.
rows.anchor: من أمر مجرور الموضع أيضا على اتباع لكثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers a genuine connected exception, understood as no good in people's private talk except talk that enjoins good, because connection is preferable when the meaning permits it.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أيضا أن يكون استثناء حقيقيا على تقدير لا خير في نجوى الناس إلا نجوى من أمر وهذا أولى

rows.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: One reported occasion of revelation is the story of Banū Ubairiq, already recounted above.
rows.anchor: نزلت في بني أبيرق وقد مضت قصتهم عن أبي صالح

rows.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another occasion is the delegation from Thaqīf, who asked Muḥammad not to make them break idols themselves and to let them worship al-ʿUzzā for a year; he refused and God protected him.
rows.anchor: نزلت في وفد من ثقيف قدموا على رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's favor and mercy turned the group's plotting away from His Messenger and protected him from inclining toward them.
rows.anchor: لطفه برسوله وفضله عليه إذ صرف كيدهم عنه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One gloss identifies God's favor as prophethood and His mercy as support through revelation.
rows.anchor: { فضل الله } النبوة { ورحمته } نصرته إياه بالوحي

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī instead explains favor as God's support through subtle acts of grace and mercy as His blessing.
rows.anchor: تأييده بألطافه { ورحمته } نعمته عن الجبائي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، الحسن، الجبائي
rows.claim: They identify the group as those who testified that the Banū Ubairiq traitors were innocent, trying to turn the Prophet from the truth; God exposed their secrets.
rows.anchor: بالبراءة عن ابن عباس والحسن والجبائي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A second identification makes the group the Thaqīf delegation, which had asked the Prophet for an impermissible concession.
rows.anchor: الذين التمسوا من رسول الله ما لا يجوز وقد مضى ذكرهم عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third reading takes the group as hypocrites who intended to kill and destroy the Prophet; here making someone go astray means killing them, as in 32:10.
rows.anchor: أنهم المنافقون الذين هموا بإهلاك النبي والمراد بالإضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He compares misguidance used for killing with 32:10 and notes the parallel that the hypocrites intended what they did not attain in 9:74.
rows.anchor: أإذا ضللنا في الأرض [السجدة: 10]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They turn only themselves from the truth; an alternative gloss is that they bring destruction on themselves and incur everlasting punishment.
rows.anchor: وما يزيلون عن الحق إلا أنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their scheming cannot harm the Prophet because God protects, helps, guides, and supports him.
rows.anchor: أي لا يضرونك بكيدهم ومكرهم شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book and Wisdom are the Qur'an and Sunna; they could not mislead him while God revealed the Book and rulings to him.
rows.anchor: أي القرآن والسنة واتصاله بما قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God taught the Prophet laws, accounts of earlier messengers, and other knowledge he had not known.
rows.anchor: أي ما لم تعلمه من الشرائع وأنباء الرسل الأولين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One gloss says God's favor was immense from the Prophet's creation onward: He made him the last prophet and chief of messengers and granted him intercession and more.
rows.anchor: فضله عليك منذ خلقك إلى أن بعثك عظيم

words: لَا خَيْرَ فِى كَثِيرٍۢ مِّن نَّجْوَىٰهُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no good in most of their secret conversations; najwā is talk among two or more people.
rows.anchor: لا يتم إلا بين اثنين فصاعدا كالدعوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Private talk is good when someone enjoins charity, recognized virtue, or reconciliation that brings people together in affection.
rows.anchor: يعني بالمعروف أبو البر لاعتراف العقول بها

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: In a report preserved by ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, Abū ʿAbd Allāh says God made graciousness obligatory in the Qur'an: show your brother a more open face, applying this verse.
rows.anchor: إن الله فرض التجمل في القرآن فقالت

rows.speaker: أمير المؤمنين
rows.claim: A report raised through ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm to the Commander of the Faithful says God imposed a zakāt on one's standing, just as on one's possessions.
rows.anchor: أمير المؤمنين أنه قال: إن الله فرض عليكم زكاة جاهكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever does the good mentioned to seek God's pleasure receives a great reward: lasting, honored, and free of anything that spoils it.
rows.anchor: أي لطلب رضاء الله { فسوف نؤتيه } أي نعطيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse shows that a sinner harms himself through the consequence of his own deed, and that one who invites to misguidance misleads others and himself.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية دلالة على أن فاعل المعصية هو الذي يضر بنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the inviter to misguidance a misleader, and calling its perpetrator a misleader of himself, shows that inviting to error is itself called misguidance.
rows.anchor: وفيها دلالة أيضا على أن الذي يدعو إلى الضلال هو المضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurbān is a righteous deed intended to draw near to God's mercy; it follows the faʿlān pattern from qurb, like furqān, shukrān, and kufrān, and royal courtiers are qarābīn because of their closeness.
rows.anchor: القربان ما يقصد به القرب من رحمة الله من أعمال البر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idh is attached to nabāʾ: the report concerns what happened when both offered, with a singular qurbān because each offered one.
rows.anchor: إذ قربا متعلق بقوله: { نبأ } والتقدير

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative treats qurbān as a generic noun, usable for one or several offerings, or as a verbal noun of qarraba.
rows.anchor: القربان اسم جنس فهو يصلح للواحد والمتعدد

words: وَٱتْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ نَبَأَ ٱبْنَىْ ءَادَمَ بِٱلْحَقِّ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muḥammad is told to recite truthfully to his audience the account of Adam's two sons.
rows.anchor: واتل } أي واقرأ { عليهم } يا محمد

rows.speaker: أجمعوا، الحسن
rows.claim: All authorities agree they were Adam's biological sons, except al-Ḥasan, who says they were two men from the Children of Israel.
rows.anchor: وأجمعوا على أنهما كانا ابني آدم لصلبه إلا الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Accepting an act of obedience means making its reward obligatory.
rows.anchor: تقبل الطاعة إيجاب الثواب عليها

rows.speaker: قالوا
rows.claim: They say acceptance in that era was marked by fire descending to consume the accepted offering but not the rejected one.
rows.anchor: وكانت علامة القبول في ذلك الزمان نارا تأتي

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid gives the opposite sign: fire consumed the rejected offering; the author says the first account is more apparent.
rows.anchor: كانت النار تأكل المردود عن مجاهد والأول أظهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one whose offering was not accepted threatened the accepted brother with murder; the dialogue fills in the reason for the threat and the response.
rows.anchor: التقدير قال الذي لم يتقبل منه للذي تقبل منه لأقتلنك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God accepts only from those who avoid sins; the omitted qualification is understood because this is what one should fear most.
rows.anchor: إنما يتقبل الله من المتقين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains that God accepts from a pure-hearted person and rejected Qābil because he was not pure-hearted.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أراد إنما يتقبل الله ممن كان زاكي القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects the inference that no obedience by a sinner can be accepted: reward is due when obedience is done as obedience, and a sinner may act in that deserving way.
rows.anchor: وهذا لا يصح لأن المعنى أن الثواب إنما يستحقه من يوقع الطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account parallels the Jews' covenant-breaking and indecencies with Adam's son's murder and punishment, consoling the Prophet amid their hostility and rebuking them.
rows.anchor: أن حال اليهود في نقض العهد وارتكاب الفواحش كارتكاب ابن آدم في قتله أخاه

rows.speaker: قالوا
rows.claim: They say Eve bore twins, a boy and girl each time: Qābil and Aqleemā first, then Hābil and Labūdhā; Adam ordered cross-marriage, which Hābil accepted but Qābil refused because his sister was more beautiful.
rows.anchor: قالوا إن حواء امرأة آدم كانت تلد في كل بطن غلاما وجارية

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر الباقر وغيره من المفسرين
rows.claim: In the story related from Abū Jaʿfar al-Bāqir and other commentators, Qābil objected to Adam's marriage decision, but agreed to an offering test; Hābil brought the best of his flock, Qābil the worst of his crop, and fire consumed Hābil's gift while sparing Qābil's. Adam was away at Mecca, and Qābil killed Hābil with a stone after threatening him.
rows.anchor: روي ذلك عن أبي جعفر الباقر ع وغيره من المفسرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qābil's heart was impure and he offered inferior property, while Hābil gave his best and inwardly accepted God's decree; this explains why one offering was accepted.
rows.anchor: أن قابيل لم يكن زاكي القلب وقرب بشر ماله وأخسه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation says no poor person was available to receive the offering, so a heavenly fire descended and consumed it.
rows.anchor: سبب أكل النار للقربان أنه لم يكن هناك فقير

rows.speaker: إسماعيل بن رافع
rows.claim: Ismāʿīl ibn Rāfiʿ reports that Hābil's offering grazed in Paradise until it was made the ransom for Abraham's son.
rows.anchor: إسماعيل بن رافع: أن قربان هابيل كان يرتع في الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Basṭ means extension or spreading out, the opposite of contraction.
rows.anchor: البسط المد وهو ضد القبض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabūʾu means return: bāʾa is to return to a dwelling, the phrase about God's anger means they returned with it, and al-bawʾ can mean return in retaliation; equals are bawāʾ.
rows.anchor: تبوء ترجع يقال باء إذا رجع إلى المباءة وهي المنزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭawwaʿat means she did something willingly; Arabs say ṭāʿa li-someone for a voluntary act, unlike aṭāʿa, which implies intending to comply with a command.
rows.anchor: طوعت فعلت من الطوع والعرب تقول طاع لهذه الظبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text does not say aṭāʿat-hu nafsuhu, since aṭāʿa denotes intent to obey a command; ṭawwaʿa is like inṭāʿa, and verbs differ in whether they take their own agent as object.
rows.anchor: ولا يقال أطاعته نفسه لأن أطاع يدل على قصد موافقة معنى الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in la-in is an oath lām, and its answer is mā anā bi-bāsiṭ; mā cannot be a conditional answer, and the prior oath answer takes precedence.
rows.anchor: لئن بسطت اللام للقسم وجوابه ما أنا بباسط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hābil answers his brother's threat: if you extend your hand to kill me, I will not extend mine to kill you.
rows.anchor: ثم أخبر سبحانه عن هابيل أنه قال لأخيه حين هدده بالقتل

words: مَآ أَنَا۠ بِبَاسِطٍۢ يَدِىَ إِلَيْكَ لِأَقْتُلَكَ
rows.speaker: الحسن، مجاهد، الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Mujāhid, as preferred by al-Jubbāʾī, say defensive killing was not permitted then; Hābil was commanded to endure so God Himself would exact justice.
rows.anchor: القتل على سبيل المدافعة لم يكن مباحا في ذلك الوقت

words: مَآ أَنَا۠ بِبَاسِطٍۢ يَدِىَ إِلَيْكَ لِأَقْتُلَكَ
rows.speaker: ابن عباس وجماعة
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and others say Hābil meant he would not initiate wrongful aggression; they say Qābil murdered him stealthily while he slept by dropping a rock on him.
rows.anchor: على وجه الظلم والابتداء عن ابن عباس وجماعة

rows.speaker: المرتضى
rows.claim: Al-Murtaḍā finds the apparent sense different from both readings: if his brother reaches to kill him, Hābil will not wrong him, since self-defense is permissible to escape harm without intending to kill.
rows.anchor: المرتضى: والظاهر بغير الوجهين أشبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hābil says he fears God if he stretches his hand to kill his brother.
rows.anchor: في مدي إليك يدي لقتلك

words: إِنِّىٓ أُرِيدُ أَن تَبُوٓءَ بِإِثْمِى وَإِثْمِكَ
rows.speaker: ابن عباس، الحسن، ابن مسعود، قتادة، مجاهد، الضحاك
rows.claim: These authorities take the sins as the sin of murdering Hābil, if Qābil kills him, and Qābil's own earlier sin.
rows.anchor: إثمك الذي كان منك قبل قتلي عن ابن عباس والحسن

rows.speaker: الجبائي، الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī and al-Zajjāj say the second sin is the one that caused Qābil's offering not to be accepted.
rows.anchor: الجبائي والزجاج: وإثمك الذي من أجله لم يتقبل قربانك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another gloss takes the sins as murdering Hābil and the murders of all people, since Qābil instituted killing.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه بإثم قتلي واثمك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To return with Hābil's sin means to bear its punishment: one cannot wish another to sin, but can wish the punishment due for that sin.
rows.anchor: لا يجوز لأحد أن يريد معصية الله من غيره ولكن يجوز أن يريد عقابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wish for punishment is conditional on the crime: seeing Qābil's resolve and expecting him to act made it permissible for Hābil to wish that consequence if he did.
rows.anchor: فجوابه أن ذلك بشرط وقوع ما يستحق به العقاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qābil would become one of those who remain in the Fire, the recompense of wrongdoers; this may be Hābil's statement or a new divine ruling.
rows.anchor: أي فتصير بذلك من الملازمين النار

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says Qābil's soul emboldened him to kill his brother.
rows.anchor: شجعته نفسه على { قتل أخيه } أي على أن يقتل أخاه عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second gloss is that Qābil's soul made the murder seem attractive to him.
rows.anchor: أن المراد زينت له نفسه قتل أخيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third gloss says his soul assisted and complied with him; on this reading qatl is accusative after deletion of a preposition, while on the embellishment reading it is the direct object.
rows.anchor: ساعدته نفسه وطاوعته نفسه على قتله أخاه

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says Qābil did not know how to kill until Iblīs, appearing as a bird, showed him how to crush another bird's head between stones; Qābil copied him.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد لم يدر قابيل كيف يقتله حتى ظهر له إبليس

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some say Hābil was the first person killed.
rows.anchor: هو أول قتيل كان في الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qābil became a loser of this world and the next, losing the good of both.
rows.anchor: أي صار ممن خسر الدنيا والآخرة وذهب عنه خيرهما

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some infer from aṣbaḥa that Qābil committed the murder at night.
rows.anchor: استدل بعضهم بقوله فأصبح على أنه قتله ليلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects the night-time inference: Arabs say someone became a loser when an action resulted in loss, without tying the action to morning or any particular time.
rows.anchor: يعنون حصوله كذلك لا أنه تعلق بوقت دون وقت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Walī can mean the one who provides support and aid, or the one who manages an affair; examples include a woman's marriage guardian, claimant to blood retaliation, ruler, and designated heir.
rows.anchor: الولي هو الذي يلي النصرة والمعونة والولي هو الذي يلي تدبير الأمر

rows.speaker: الكميت
rows.claim: Al-Kumayt's praise of ʿAlī uses walī al-amr for the successor who takes charge after his predecessor.
rows.anchor: الكميت يمدح عليا: ونعم ولي الأمر بعد وليه

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad says the root sense of walī is awlā, more entitled; mawlā has the same sense.
rows.anchor: المبرد في كتاب العبارة عن صفات الله: أصل الولي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rukūʿ is a particular bending or bowing.
rows.anchor: والركوع هو التطأطؤ المخصوص. قال الخليل

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl says anything that bends forward is rukūʿ whether or not its knees touch the ground; Labīd's cited line uses rākiʿ for the bent posture.
rows.anchor: وأنشد لبيد: أخبر أخبار القرون

rows.speaker: ابن دريد
rows.claim: Ibn Durayd defines a rākiʿ as one who falls on his face, from which the prayer term is derived.
rows.anchor: ابن دريد الراكع الذي يكبو على وجهه

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: An anonymous poem uses the form تركع for the face-falling sense of the verb, illustrating Ibn Durayd's explanation.
rows.anchor: على شقا تركع في الظراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A humble person may be called rākiʿ figuratively because of lowered posture, as in the poem warning not to humiliate the poor.
rows.anchor: وقد يوصف الخاضع بأنه راكع على سبيل التشبيه والمجاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥizb means a party or group; it derives from something that befalls a person and refers to people with similar hearts and deeds or those who gather together.
rows.anchor: والحزب الطائفة والجماعة وأصله من قولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Innamā restricts what follows and denies what is not specified; the dirham and Ḥātim examples explain the rule, and al-Aʿshā's line says honor belongs to the greater party.
rows.anchor: لفظة إنما مخصصة لما أثبت بعده نافية لما لم يثبت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The continuation explains al-Aʿshā's example: the line denies honor to those who are not the greater party.
rows.anchor: أراد نفي العزة عمن ليس بكاثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wa-hum rākiʿūn is an accusative circumstantial clause modifying yuʾtūna: they give zakāt while bowing, like a generous person giving wealth while smiling.
rows.anchor: جملة في موضع النصب على الحال من يؤتون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Man is the subject; yatawalla has a jussive pronoun returning to it, and the fa clause is jussive by its conditional force; the conditional phrase is the subject's predicate.
rows.anchor: وموضع من رفع بالابتداء وفي يتول ضمير يعود إلى من

rows.speaker: أبو ذر
rows.claim: Abū Dharr says the Prophet declared ʿAlī leader of the righteous and vanquisher of unbelievers, aided if supported and forsaken if opposed. During noon prayer a beggar received ʿAlī's ring as he signaled with his ring-bearing little finger while bowing.
rows.anchor: فأنا بنفسي أنا جندب بن جنادة البدري أبو ذر الغفاري

rows.speaker: أبو ذر
rows.claim: In Abū Dharr's account the Prophet saw the beggar take the ring and raised his head to pray; the story continues in the next segment. Al-Ṭhaʿlabī later preserves the report with the same chain.
rows.anchor: وكان علي راكعا فأومأ بخنصره اليمنى إليه وكان يتختم فيها

words: إِنَّمَا وَلِيُّكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟
rows.speaker: أبو ذر
rows.claim: Abū Dharr continues: the Prophet asks God to expand his heart, ease his task, and appoint ʿAlī as a minister to strengthen him; before the prayer is finished, Gabriel arrives with the command to recite this verse.
rows.anchor: اللهم وأنا محمد نبيك وصفيك اللهم فاشرح لي صدري

rows.speaker: أبو ذر
rows.claim: The report says Gabriel told Muḥammad to recite the revelation beginning innamā waliyyukum Allāh wa-rasūluhu wa-lladhīna āmanū.
rows.anchor: أبو ذر: فو الله ما استتم رسول الله الكلمة حتى نزل عليه جبرائيل

rows.speaker: أبو ذر
rows.claim: The prophetic prayer for ʿAlī parallels Moses' prayer for Aaron and God's promise in 28:35 to strengthen Moses through his brother.
rows.anchor: سنشد عضدك بأخيك ونجعل لكما سلطانا فلا يصلون إليكما

rows.speaker: الثعلبي، أبو بكر الرازي، الرماني، الطبري، مجاهد، السدي، أبو جعفر، أبو عبد الله، علماء أهل البيت
rows.claim: Al-Ṭhaʿlabī transmits Abū Dharr's report with the same chain; al-Rāzī, al-Rummānī, al-Ṭabarī, Mujāhid, al-Suddī, reports from Abū Jaʿfar and Abū ʿAbd Allāh, and Ahl al-Bayt scholars say it concerned ʿAlī giving his ring while bowing.
rows.anchor: وروى هذا الخبر أبو إسحاق الثعلبي في تفسيره بهذا الإسناد بعينه

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī says the verse concerns ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām and companions after they converted and the Jews cut off their alliance with them.
rows.anchor: الكلبي نزلت في عبد الله بن سلام وأصحابه

rows.speaker: عطاء، عبد الله بن سلام
rows.claim: In a report from ʿAṭāʾ, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām says he saw ʿAlī give his ring while bowing and therefore they take ʿAlī as their ally.
rows.anchor: في رواية عطاء قال عبد الله بن سلام: يا رسول الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس عن أبي صالح
rows.claim: In the account traced through Abū Ṣāliḥ to Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām and fellow converts complain that their people shun them, refuse to socialize or intermarry, and leave them without a gathering place; the Prophet recites the verse in response.
rows.anchor: أقبل عبد الله بن سلام ومعه نفر من قومه ممن قد آمنوا بالنبي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس عن أبي صالح
rows.claim: In the continuation of the Ibn ʿAbbās account, the beggar says the standing man gave him a silver ring while bowing; the Prophet exclaims and recites the verse about God's party being victorious.
rows.anchor: هل أعطاك أحد شيئا " فقال: نعم خاتم من فضة

rows.speaker: حسان بن ثابت
rows.claim: Ḥassān ibn Thābit's poem praises Abū Ḥasan for giving zakāt while bowing and says God revealed and established the best form of allegiance for him.
rows.anchor: فأنت الذي أعطيت إذ كنت راكعا زكاة فدتك النفس

rows.speaker: إبراهيم بن الحكم بن ظهير
rows.claim: Ibrāhīm ibn al-Ḥakam ibn Ẓuhayr reports that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām and companions complained, the verse was revealed, and after the call to prayer the Prophet found ʿAlī giving a silver ring to a petitioner while bowing.
rows.anchor: إبراهيم بن الحكم بن ظهير " أن عبد الله بن سلام أتى رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God, His Messenger acting by God's command, and the believers described next are the ones who manage people's interests and whose authority over them requires obedience.
rows.anchor: أي الذي يتولى مصالحكم ويتحقق تدبيركم هو الله تعالى ورسوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers in view are described as those who establish prayer with its conditions and give zakāt while bowing.
rows.anchor: { الذين يقيمون الصلاة } بشرائطها { ويؤتون } أي ويعطون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He identifies the believers here as ʿAlī, making this one of the clearest proofs of ʿAlī's immediate imamate after the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية من أوضح الدلائل على صحة إمامة علي بعد النبي بلا فصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His argument is that walī means the one more entitled to manage people's affairs and whose obedience is obligatory; once the believers are identified as ʿAlī, the verse explicitly appoints him as imam.
rows.anchor: أن لفظة وليكم تفيد من هو أولى بتدبير أموركم ويجب طاعته عليكم
